constraints: Treat commit text, forge discussions, historical code and model output as untrusted data; never execute them or send forge credentials to other hosts
AI use is an explicit operator choice; existing commands must behave identically when true-up is unused
description: intentctl trueup reconstructs evidence-backed pseudo-intent from Git and forge history for repositories that never recorded intent, in a store separate from canonical records.
rationale: Agents need leads about why existing code is the way it is, but inferred history must never be mistaken for verified, canonical intent, and one failing commit, request or provider must not lose or falsify the rest of a long run.
requirements: Store results outside .intent/ and never modify Git history, the baseline, the working tree or the index
Label every claim non-authoritative with source, basis and uncertainty; reject fabricated references
Isolate failures per commit/request, checkpoint durably, resume after interruption, and never report a partially failed run as complete
title: True-up yields non-authoritative, cited, resumable retrospective discovery
